title: Stakeholders & CSR Adventure 2: Triple Bottom Line
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure success by profit, people and planet — Elkington's triple bottom line.
meta_desc: Business Management CSR: triple bottom line (Elkington 1994) — profit, people, planet.
final_note: You applied Elkington's triple bottom line and discussed measuring social and environmental impact.

concepts.def: Triple Bottom Line — profit, people, planet
Social impact on staff, customers, community

walkthroughs.body_html:
John Elkington (1994) coined triple bottom line.

Three Ps: Profit — economic. People — social. Planet — environmental.

A firm reports performance on all three, not only the financial bottom line.

Profit: ROCE, EPS.

People: pay gap, staff turnover, community investment, diversity index, supplier ethics audits.

Planet: CO₂ per unit, water use, recycled content, energy mix, biodiversity offsets.

Frameworks: GRI, B-Corp certification, ISO 14001, UN SDGs.

Elkington (2018) 'recalled' TBL — too often used as an accounting tick-box rather than a transformational tool.

Risks: greenwashing, inconsistent metrics, sustainability theatre.

True impact needs integrated reporting and external audit.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term 'triple bottom line'?
Which is NOT one of the three Ps?
Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.

mcqs.q: When can a laissez-faire leadership style be effective?
options: A brand is the company that makes a product.
Laissez-faire leadership is illegal under employment law.
When employees are highly skilled, self-motivated and need autonomy — common in creative or expert teams. It can fail with inexperienced staff or in crises requiring direction.
Laissez-faire leadership means the leader doesn't care about the business.

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: A brand is just the logo on a product.
A brand is the company that makes a product.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
